papers.title: Blind Precise Assembly: Proprioceptive Sim-to-Real Peg-in-Hole for Diverse Parts
papers.summary: Every robot already carries high-resolution contact sensors: its own joints. Legged robots and humanoids exploit them to walk, run, and track whole-body motions without vision, but there the contacts are large and forceful. papers.title: CocoRNA: Collective RNA Design with Cooperative Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Designing RNA sequences that reliably fold into specific secondary structures is essential for understanding their biological functions but remains a challenging computational problem. We propose CocoRNA, a cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for RNA inverse design. CocoRNA simplifies the design task by decomposing it into smaller sub-problems, each solved collaboratively by multiple agents. papers.title: Not All Actions Contribute Equally: Learning Precise Progress Estimation from Imprecise Demonstrations
papers.summary: Progress estimators play an essential role in providing dense reward signals for reinforcement learning in robotic manipulation, but accurately assessing task progress can be much challenging. Existing methods heavily rely on expert data and naively assume that all actions within a demonstration contribute to task success. papers.title: Learning Robot Metareasoning: Adaptive Computation Budgets for Real-Time Control
papers.summary: Planning while moving faces an historical trade-off between deliberation and reactivity. A planner running concurrently with execution needs time to compute, so the robot must commit to an open-loop action chunk for that duration: a longer commitment buys a better plan at the cost of feedback frequency. papers.title: JAXtari: High-Throughput and Easy-to-Modify Arcade Learning Environment
papers.summary: The Arcade Learning Environment (ALE) has been a cornerstone of Deep Reinforcement Learning research, providing a standardized benchmark for evaluating general agents. However, its lack of native support for object-extraction and environment modification restricts research into evaluating whether agents learn robust causal models or rely on brittle visual heuristics. papers.title: RL-Guided Temporal Localization for Dual-Channel Retrieval in Long-Horizon Agent Memory
papers.summary: Time-aware retrieval is crucial for long-horizon LLM agents to effectively leverage ever-growing long-term memory. Existing methods focus on lexical or semantic similarity, leading to target memories being crowded out by temporally mismatched yet semantically similar candidates. papers.title: Analyzing Occupational Gender Bias across the LLM Training Lifecycle
papers.summary: Post-training is widely assumed to reduce the social biases language models inherit from pretraining, yet direct evidence for this assumption remains mixed. In this paper, we examine how gender disparities evolve across the language modeling pipeline. papers.title: Reason-guided Human Reward Modeling for Preference-based Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) policies optimized for task rewards may produce behaviors that are efficient but misaligned with human expectations, safety preferences, or intent. papers.title: Reinforcement Learning Based Multi-Terrain Adaptive Whole-Body Control for a Quadruped Manipulator
papers.summary: Legged robots equipped with manipulators offer promising capabilities for loco-manipulation tasks in unstructured environments. However, achieving task-consistent end-effector behavior during locomotion remains challenging due to terrain-induced disturbances and the strong coupling between locomotion and manipulation, particularly for small-scale quadruped platforms. papers.summary: In many real-world scenarios we need to consider formal requirements, such as safety and constraint compliance, to deploy Reinforcement Learning (RL) agents. In this paper we introduce RecReg, a safe RL framework capable of enforcing non-Markovian regular safety properties via recovery-based shielding. papers.title: No Eyes, No Problem: What Does Touch Contribute to Blind Baoding Ball Manipulation?
papers.summary: Humans manipulate objects within their hands through touch alone with remarkable ease, but for robots, achieving sustained real-world manipulation without vision remains an open challenge. papers.title: Language Models Learn to Improve Language Models
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to automate AI research, including language-model (LM) development, offering a potential path toward recursive self-improvement. papers.summary: Multimodal preference alignment often follows a score-based RLHF pipeline: a reward model is first trained to learn human preferences, then used to score on-policy responses and optimize the response model's generation. papers.summary: In a hierarchical multi-agent system, a Leader assigns tasks and subagents carry them out. Jointly training the Leader and the subagents is difficult because a final answer gives only indirect feedback to the subagents. papers.title: SimpleVLN: Towards Simple and Frontier Vision-Language Navigation
papers.summary: Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) requires embodied agents to ground language in visual observations and make long-horizon decisions. Existing methods often address these demands through task-specific architectures. papers.title: Proportionality in Ranking Compression
papers.summary: Motivated by applications in reinforcement learning from human feedback, we consider a setting where a given collection of rankings needs to be compressed into a smaller collection of rankings. papers.summary: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) has substantially improved Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs, but its outcome-level rewards provide only sparse supervision. papers.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards has become a scalable post-training paradigm for large language models. papers.title: BeJEPA: A Goal-Conditioned Humanoid Behavior World Model via Unsupervised RL
papers.summary: Humanoid control requires coordinating whole-body posture with position and heading in the world frame. Mainstream controllers imitate trajectories in the root frame, but struggle to regain the target world pose after displacement. papers.summary: Real-world frontend development requires agents to compose reproduction, generation, modification, and repair over an evolving application state. papers.summary: The learning algorithm view of in-context learning (ICL) studies how fixed-parameter Transformers learn from supplied examples. papers.summary: Automated research ideation has advanced rapidly, with multi-agent workflows that generate whole research ideas end to end. papers.summary: Reinforcement learning improves diffusion models using rewards on generated images, but repeated denoising and gradient estimation make training expensive. papers.summary: Small variations in prompt characteristics can meaningfully alter the semantics, tone, and contextual assumptions of large language model outputs. papers.summary: Contact locations and interaction forces are critical for contact-rich robot manipulation but are often ambiguous from vision alone. papers.summary: Open-ended tool agents can complete the same objective through different tool paths, and their quality depends jointly on the interaction trace, environment state, and final artifacts, so such tasks rarely admit an executable ground-truth reward. papers.summary: Long rollout windows make reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) expensive, yet simply shortening them can remove the correctness signal: when every single-problem rollout truncates before an answer, group-relative accuracy advantages vanish. papers.title: Sample-Efficient Reinforcement Learning for Policy Improvement via Flow-Reversed Action Anchors
papers.summary: Generalist robot policies offer strong behavioral priors, but achieving deployment-level reliability and throughput remains difficult. Reinforcement learning (RL) can improve these policies, yet its effectiveness is constrained by the cost of online interaction. papers.title: Causal Edit Serialization
papers.summary: Standard autoregressive language models generate text sequentially, but revision requires referring back to tokens in the input context or those already generated. Causal Edit Serialization (CES) is introduced as a framework for expressing such revisions within the same causal token stream. papers.summary: Scalable approaches to learning neural dynamical systems have placed diffusion, flow matching, and few-step generators in flow maps at the forefront of generative modeling. papers.summary: Forecasting an unresolved event requires finding relevant evidence and deciding how strongly it supports each outcome. papers.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for improving the reasoning capabilities of LLMs. However, the role of supervised fine-tuning (SFT) data in enabling effective downstream RL remains underexplored. papers.summary: Real-world post-training of generalist robot policies faces two challenges: partial observability makes action selection ambiguous, while offline post-training methods delay feedback from deployment experience.
